Here is a concise, ready-to-use 12-week summary of the complete program, integrating strength with cycle-aware adjustments, cardio, HIIT, plyometrics/power, plyometric day, nutrition, and flow-day modifications. The plan assumes a 28-day cycle with flow days at the start of each cycle (days 1–3). Start date: 2026-06-01. Day naming is relative to week of plan; you can map to actual calendar days as needed.

Core structure
- Weekly lifting days: 4 primary lifting days (A, B, C, D) plus a dedicated plyometric/power day (F) and a HIIT/metCon day (E) and optional cardio days (B, C, D as per your schedule).
- Cardio: 3 sessions weekly with a mix of steady-state, tempo, and intervals. Schedule avoids heavy fatigue on flow days; adjust to fit client’s calendar.
- Plyometric/Power: 1 day per week, lower volume, cycle-aware, with progressive exposure.
- HIIT/MetCon: 1 day per week, metabolic conditioning, cycle-aware, non-flow friendly.
- Nutrition: cycle-aware daily targets with higher carb on heavy training days, electrolyte focus, and micronutrients to support cramps and fatigue.
- Flow-day strategy: reduce load, avoid heavy Valsalva, low-impact work, tempo/paused variations, pelvic-floor activation.

Phase 1: Foundational Strength and Technique (Weeks 1–4)
- Objective: build movement quality, establish baseline loads, develop technique, and create a foundation for progressive overload.

Weeks 1–2 (Starting 2026-06-01)
- Day A – Lower (Squat emphasis)
  - Back Squat: 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute Bridge/ Hip Thrust: 3x10
  - Core: dead bug 3x12 per side
- Day B – Upper (Push/Pull)
  - Bench or Floor Press: 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Bent-Over Row: 3x8
  - Overhead Press: 3x6
  - Incline DB Flyes: 3x10
  - Pallof Press: 3x10 per side
- Day C – Lower (Hinge emphasis)
  - Deadlift or Trap Bar: 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Front Squat or Goblet Squat: 3x8
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8
  - Lunges/Step-Ups: 3x8 per leg
  - Plank variations: 3x30–45s
- Day D – Accessory/Tempo & Core
  - Tempo work on main lifts (3-0-3-0 to 3-0-2-0)
  - Carry variations: Farmer’s Carry 3x40–60s
  - Glute/Hip work and pelvic-floor activation
  - Mobility and breathing

Weeks 3–4 (Deload/refine)
- Reduce volume ~10–15%; maintain technique focus.
- Keep core and pelvic-floor activation, allow adaptation, and prep for Phase 2.

Phase 2: Hypertrophy-Plus-Strength with Elevated Intensity (Weeks 5–8)
- Objective: Build stronger neural drive and hypertrophy while preserving mechanics and pelvic health. Heavier loading with adjusted volume.

Weeks 5–6
- Day A – Lower (Squat emphasis, heavier)
  - Back Squat: 5x5 at 80–85% 1RM
  - Paused/Tempo Squats: 3x4 at 70–75%
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x8
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute Bridge/Hip Thrust: 3x10
  - Core: anti-rotation hold 3x30–40s
- Day B – Upper (Push/Pull, heavier)
  - Bench Press: 5x5 at 80–85% 1RM
  - Barbell Row/T-Bar Row: 4x6
  - Overhead Press: 4x5 at 70–75%
  - Weighted Chin-Ups/Pull-Ups: 4x6–8
  - Lateral Raises: 3x12
- Day C – Lower (Hinge emphasis)
  - Deadlift: 5x4 at 80–85%
  - Front Squat: 3x6
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6–8
  - Lunges/Step-Ups: 3x8 per leg
  - Plank variations: 60s
- Day D – Accessory/Conditioning
  - Tempo core work: 3x12–15
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x40–60s
  - Mobility and pelvic-floor activation: 10–15 minutes

Weeks 7–8
- Day A – Lower (Intensified)
  - Back Squat: 5x3 at 88–92% 1RM
  - Pause/Tempo Squats: 3x3 at 75–80%
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6
  - Glute/Ham Raise or Tempo Glute Bridge: 3x8
  - Core: side planks 3x40s per side
- Day B – Upper (Intensified)
  - Bench Press: 5x3 at 88–92% 1RM
  - Bent-Over Row/DB Row: 4x6–8
  - Overhead Press: 4x5 at 75–80%
  - Weighted Chin-Ups/Pull-Ups: 4x6–8
  - Triceps work: 3x8
- Day C – Lower (Hinge)
  - Deadlift: 5x3 at 88–92% 1RM
  - Front Squat: 3x6
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6–8
  - Lunges/Step-Ups: 3x6–8
  - Core: 50s hollow holds
- Day D – Accessory/Conditioning
  - Pallof Press: 3x12
  - Farmer’s Carry: 3x50–70s
  - Mobility and pelvic-floor work: 15 minutes
- Flow-day adjustments: maintain flow-day reductions; substitute with tempo/paused variations if needed.

Phase 3: Peak Strength and Conditioning (Weeks 9–12)
- Objective: Maximize strength with controlled volume and lower reps; maintain technique and recovery around flow days.

Weeks 9–10
- Day A – Lower (Squat emphasis)
  - Back Squat: 5x3 at 85–90%
  - Paused/Tempo Squats: 3x3
  - Romanian Deadlift: 3x6
  - Bulgarian Split Squat: 3x6
  - Core: side planks 3x30–45s per side
- Day B – Upper (Push/Pull)
  - Bench Press: 5x3 at 85–90%
  - Barbell Row: 3x6
  - Overhead Press: 3x5
  - Weighted Chin-Ups: 3x6
  - Triceps work: 3x8
- Day C – Lower (Hinge)
  - Deadlift/Sumo Deadlift: 4x3 at 85–90%
  - Front Squat: 3x6
  - Hip Thrust: 3x6
  - RDL: 3x6
  - Core: hollow holds 3x30–40s
- Day D – Accessory/Conditioning
  - Pallof Press: 3x12
  - Farmers Carry: 3x50–70s
  - Mobility and pelvic-floor work: 15 minutes
- Day E – HIIT/MetCon (40–45 minutes) integrated as per plan

Weeks 9–12 continued
- Week 9–10 focus: push max through phase with controlled progression; reduce ancillary fatigue
- Week 11–12: Deload and testing preparation
  - Week 11: begin deloading volume by 20–40%
  - Week 12: testing week only if client is rested and symptoms are well-managed; perform 1RM tests (squat, bench, deadlift) with ramp-up warm-ups and safe attempt progression.

Deload and testing (Weeks 11–12)
- Week 11: Deload across all lifts; maintain technique with lighter loads
- Week 12: Optional 1RM testing window
  - If testing: plan 3 testing days (Squat, Bench, Deadlift) with ample rest and a reduced total weekly volume, as described in the 1RM testing guidance.

Cardio and metabolic conditioning
- 3 cardio sessions weekly (steady-state, tempo, intervals) with cycle-aware adjustments
- HIIT day on Week 9–12 maintained at tolerable levels; Flow-day adjustments applied
- Plyometric/Power day on Week 9–12 integrated with strength work; keep flow-day safety

Plyometric/Power Day (Day F)
- Lower volume, high quality, cycle-aware
- Weeks 1–4: introduce gradually
- Weeks 5–8: increase height/volume modestly
- Weeks 9–12: peak power exposures with careful dose management

PUSH for Test Week (1RM end of Phase 3)
- If desired, perform a 1RM testing block during Week 12 or Week 11–12 window with well-timed warm-ups and readiness checks
- Reassess 1RM resets for Phase 4 planning

Optional testing and progression plan
- If you prefer, perform a 3–5RM test as a surrogate and estimate 1RM for each lift
- Alternatively, use daily velocity-based autoregulation for progression rather than fixed percentages if equipment is available (e.g., app-based velocity tracking)

Flow-day management
- Flow days 1–3: reduced load, tempo work, breathing and pelvic-floor activation
- Outside flow days: full program intensity and volume
- Adjust weekly plan if symptoms worsen: swap in more rest, reduce volume, or shift HIIT/plyometric intensity as needed

Nutritional framework (recap)
- Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day
- Carbs: 3–5 g/kg/day; higher on heavy lifting days
- Fats: remaining calories; emphasize omega-3s
- Micronutrients: magnesium 300–420 mg/day, potassium 2.5–3.5 g/day, calcium 1,000–1,200 mg/day, iron as indicated
- Hydration: 30–40 ml/kg/day plus electrolytes on long or hot sessions
- Pre/post-workout nutrition: 30–60 g carbs and 15–25 g protein pre-workout; 20–40 g protein and 40–60 g carbs post-workout

Recovery and monitoring
- Sleep: 7–9 hours
- Pelvic-floor and diaphragmatic breathing daily
- Monitoring: maintain a cycle log with flow days, symptoms, RPE, and training performance
- Red flags: sudden sharp pain, dizziness, chest pain, or marked functional impairment require medical review

Deliverables you may want next
- A calendarized, date-specific 12-week plan with exact daily prescriptions (lifting, cardio, HIIT, plyometrics, flow-day adjustments)
- Printable one-page weekly sheets for each phase (Weeks 1–4, 5–8, 9–12)
- A 1RM testing protocol and post-test recalibration plan
- A quick-reference flow-day cheat sheet and a video cue sheet for safe plyometrics and explosive moves

Here is a 12-week strength program that phases around her menstrual cycle, accommodating the flow days (days 1–3 of her cycle) when high-intensity, heavy Valsalva, and plyometric/Jump work should be avoided. The plan assumes a 28-day cycle with flow days at the start of each cycle. The starting date is 2026-06-01, and weeks are indexed relative to that date. If her cycle timing shifts, you can adjust by a day or two as needed.

Key assumptions and approach
- Training windows:
  - Flow days (approx. days 1–3 of the cycle): lighter, low-impact, no heavy Valsalva, no high-impact plyos. Emphasize technique, mobility, core stabilization, and submaximal loads.
  - Outside flow window: normal strength training with progressive overload.
- Weekly cadence: 4 lifting days per week (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) with 1–2 optional conditioning/activation days (light cardio or mobility) as needed. If your schedule differs, you can shift days but keep the flow-day adaptations anchored to the cycle days.
- Intensity progression: linear progressive overload across phases with deloads every 4 weeks to accommodate hormonal and recovery needs.
- Exercise selection: primary compound lifts (squat, hinge, push, pull, loaded carries) with supportive accessories for hypertrophy and technique. Core and pelvic-floor friendly movements are emphasized, especially during flow days.
- Recovery and nutrition: emphasis on adequate protein (1.6–2.2 g/kg/day), energy intake to support training, sleep 7–9 hours, hydration, and stress management. Include deload and red flags for fatigue.

Cycle mapping
- Flow window: days 1–3 of the cycle (approx. days 1–3 of each 28-day cycle). On these days, steer away from heavy loads, limit Valsalva, avoid jumps, and prioritize technique, tempo work, breathing, and mild core work.
- Outside flow window: higher intensities, more volume, normal Valsalva as needed for lifting, and inclusion of jumps/impact where appropriate.

12-week program outline
Phase 1: Foundational Strength and Technique (Weeks 1–4)
- Objective: establish movement quality, establish baseline loads, begin progressive overload, and build aerobic capacity and pelvic-floor–friendly core.

Weeks 1–2 (Starting 2026-06-01)
Session structure (4 days/week)
- Day A (Lower: squat emphasis)
  - Back squat: 3 sets x 5 reps at ~75% 1RM
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x8 at moderate load
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x8 per leg
  - Glute bridge or hip thrust: 3x10
  - Core: dead bug 3x12 per side
- Day B (Upper: push/pull)

  - Bent-over row or DB row: 3x8
  - Overhead press (strict or push press): 3x6
  - Incline DB flyes: 3x10

  - Deadlift or trap-bar deadlift: 3x5 at ~75% 1RM
  - Front squat or goblet squat: 3x8
  - Romanian deadlift: 3x8
  - Lunges or step-ups: 3x8 per leg
  - Plank variations: 3x30–45s
- Day D (Accessory/Tempo & Core)
  - Tempo work for main lifts (e.g., 3-0-3-0), lighter loads
  - Farmer’s carry or suitcase carry: 3x40–60s
  - Band-resisted glute bridge and hip abduction/add
  - Mobility and pelvic-floor activation: 10–15 minutes

Notes for Weeks 1–2:
- Focus on technique, tempo (3-0-2-0 to 3-0-3-0 on main lifts), and steady loads.
- Flow days: treat as Day A-D with lighter intensities or substitute with unilateral work, mobility, and breath work if any session would otherwise overlap the flow constraints.

Weeks 3–4 (deload and refine)
- Slightly reduce volume or intensity (about 10–15%) to allow adaptation.
- Maintain exercise selection with emphasis on form and range of motion.
- Include one dedicated mobility session midweek if needed.

Phase 2: Hypertrophy and Strength Accumulation (Weeks 5–8)
- Objective: increase training volume with controlled progressive overload, maintain pelvic-floor/core integrity, and introduce more accessory work to support main lifts.

Weeks 5–6
- Day A (Lower: squat emphasis)
  - Back squat: 4x6 at ~75–80% 1RM

- Day D (Accessory/conditioning)
  - Tempo core work, dragon flags progressions, cable anti-rotation: 3x10–12
  - Farmer’s carry or heavy carries: 3x40–60s
  - Mobility and warm-down

Weeks 7–8 (progression)
- Increase sets for main lifts: 4–5x5 or 5x5 schemes as appropriate
- Keep accessory volume high enough to support hypertrophy and strength
- Maintain flow-day adjustments as needed

Phase 3: Peak Strength and Conditioning (Weeks 9–12)
- Objective: maximize strength with lower repetition ranges; maintain technique and recovery around flow days.

Weeks 9–10
- Day A (Lower: squat emphasis)
  - Back squat: 5x3 at 85–90% 1RM

  - Romanian deadlift: 3x6
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3x6 per leg

- Day D (Active recovery/conditioning)

Weeks 11–12 (Deload and test/retrospective)
- Reduce volume by ~40–60% across all lifts
- Reassess 1RM estimates or rep max equivalents to set-up for ongoing progression
- Optional short performance testing (e.g., 1RM back squat, 1RM bench) if appropriate and well-tolerated
- Maintain pelvic-floor supported core work and breathing routines
- End with a plan for maintenance or a new progression template after the 12 weeks based on performance and tolerance

Flow-day adjustments (applied within weeks)
- Flow days (days 1–3 of each cycle): adjust as follows
  - Reduce main lift volume by 40–60% and keep intensity moderate (e.g., 60–70% 1RM) or substitute with lighter variations:

  - Limit Valsalva and avoid high-impact jumps or plyometrics

Nutrition and recovery guidance

Notes for safety and tailoring
- If pain or dysmenorrhea worsens or if there are any new red flags (severe pelvic pain, heavy bleeding, dizziness, chest pain), pause training and reassess with the GP or a clinician.
- Adjust load based on daily energy, mood, and symptoms. It’s okay to slide a lifting day to an easier session within the week if symptoms are more intense.
- Track cycle days and symptoms to optimize session planning; use a simple log to mark flow days, intensity, and perceived exertion (RPE).
- Include progressive overload but avoid overreaching; 1–2% weekly progression in load or reps is a practical guideline.

Core daily targets (adjust to bodyweight and goals)

- Fat: the remaining calories after protein and carbs are set; fats support hormonal health and satiety.
- Estimated range for a typical recreational lifter (~60–70 kg): roughly 90–160 g protein, 180–350 g carbs, 50–90 g fat per day. Adjust downward or upward based on fat loss/gain goals and energy needs.

Cycle-phase nutrition adjustments
- Flow days (days 1–3 of cycle): fatigue and cramps may be higher. Emphasize easily digestible carbohydrates, extra hydration, and minerals to support cramps.
  - Carbs: 4–6 g/kg/day if energy is low or training intensity is reduced; prioritize low-FODMAP options if GI sensitivity is present.
  - Protein: maintain at 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day.
  - Fats: keep moderate; focus on anti-inflammatory fats.
  - Added electrolytes and minerals to manage cramps: sodium, potassium, magnesium, calcium.
- Outside flow days: standard targets with a slight energy surplus if aiming for hypertrophy or a maintenance plan if weight stability is desired.
  - Consider a slightly higher carbohydrate intake on moderate-to-high training days to support performance.

Key micronutrients linked to dysmenorrhea and fatigue (and daily targets)
- Magnesium: 300–420 mg/day (prefer magnesium glycinate or citrate for better tolerance). Supports muscle relaxation and cramps.
- Potassium: 2.5–3.5 g/day (emphasize fruits, potatoes, leafy greens). Helps with cramps and hydration balance.
- Calcium: 1,000–1,200 mg/day (dairy or fortified alternatives). May aid cramps and mood.
- Vitamin D: 600–2000 IU/day depending on sun exposure and levels; supports bone health and mood.
- Omega-3 fatty acids: 2–3 g/day EPA+DHA. Anti-inflammatory and may help cramps.

- Iron: monitor if heavy flow occurs; consider 18 mg/day supplement if iron is low or if ferritin is low (consult clinician). Fatigue with heavy flow can reflect iron loss.

Hydration and electrolyte strategy
- Baseline water: 30–40 ml/kg/day as a starting point; adjust with activity level and climate.
- Electrolyte supplementation for flow days or heavy training: 
  - Sodium: 3–5 g/day total from foods and beverages; may increase on hot days or with heavy sweating.
  - Potassium-rich foods daily: bananas, sweet potatoes, leafy greens, beans.
  - Magnesium: 300–420 mg/day as noted above.
  - If cramps are frequent, consider an electrolyte drink around workouts (contains sodium, potassium, and magnesium) especially on flow days.
- Caffeine: moderate use if tolerated; avoid late-day caffeine if it disrupts sleep, as sleep quality influences cycle-related fatigue.

- Pre-workout: 30–60 g carbs with 15–25 g protein 1–2 hours before training; adjust if flow symptoms reduce appetite.

  - Box jumps or box squat jumps: 3–4 sets x 3–5 reps (low height; soft landing). If impact sensitive, substitute with outcomes like broad jumps to moderate distance or seated countermovement jump with emphasis on height control and minimal ground contact time.
  - Squat jumps from tempo squats or jump squats with controlled tempo: 3x3–4 x 2–3 reps.
  - Lateral bounds or skater hops: 3x6–8 total contacts per side; focus on lateral power and stability.
  - Med-ball throw variations: standing overhead throws or rotational side throws with a light medicine ball; 3x6–8 throws each side.

  - 1–2 rounds of 5–6 reps velocity-focused moves (e.g., speed deadlifts with light weight, or kettlebell swings with light load) emphasizing fast bar/hip extension without technique breakdown.

Weeks 5–8 (Phase 2) progression
- Increase intensity modestly: raise jump height slightly, add one more set, or introduce a more dynamic plyometric movement (e.g., single-leg hops) if technique is solid.
- Maintain emphasis on soft landings and control to protect the spine and pelvic floor.
- If fatigue is high or flow days worsen, reduce the volume by 20–30% or substitute with non-impact plyometrics (e.g., resisted line hops with minimal vertical component).

Weeks 9–12 (Phase 3) peak and conditioning

- Red flags: sharp or joint pain during or after jumps; stop and revert to non-impact alternatives.

Guidance for a safe 1RM test window (Weeks 9–12)
- Pre-test precautions
  - Ensure she has completed all weeks of Phase 3 with consistent technique and no red flags (pain, dizziness, heavy fatigue).
  - Confirm her cycle phase; avoid testing during peak flow days (days 1–3) when symptoms are greatest. Plan the test for a time in the cycle when she typically feels best (e.g., mid-follicular or late luteal, depending on her pattern).
  - Reassess readiness: perform a last practice set at near-working weights to confirm technique and confidence.
  - Ensure a proper warm-up: general warm-up, mobility, and ramped activation for the specific lift.

Testing protocol options
- Primary lifts to test
  - Back squat 1RM
  - Bench press 1RM (or floor press if preferred to reduce shoulder risk)
  - Deadlift 1RM (conventional or sumo as per client preference)
- Alternative: if joints or fatigue are concerns, perform a 3–5RM test and convert using established estimates, or use a non-linear progression test (e.g., ramped single-rep attempts with 1–2 safe attempts per lift).

Test structure (example)
- Day 1: Squat 1RM
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes general, 5–10 minutes of specific warm-up sets (e.g., 2–3 ramping sets: 45–60% 1RM for 3–5 reps, 60–70% for 2 reps, 70–80% for 1–2 reps)
  - Single heavy attempt: attempt at ≈90–95% to gauge true max
  - If successful, proceed to 1–2 more attempts with increasing load (e.g., +2.5–5 kg) with adequate rest (3–5 minutes)
  - If failed at initial attempt, drop back and try a back-off attempt at ~85–90% to confirm a benchmark
- Day 2: Bench 1RM
  - Similar ramp-up with attention to shoulder health; manage grip width and tempo
- Day 3: Deadlift 1RM
  - Ramp-up sets; consider using straps only if necessary for grip fatigue and to protect form
- If scheduling 3 tests in 1 week is too fatiguing, consolidate into a single testing day with all three lifts, separated by ample rest (10–15 minutes between lifts) and optional alternate lifts if needed.

Safety considerations
- Avoid pain: any joint pain or aggravation during attempts warrants stopping and reverting to a submax testing approach.
- Pelvic-floor considerations: maintain breath coordination and avoid breath-holding during attempts; consider intra-abdominal pressure management strategies to reduce strain on dysmenorrhea symptoms.
- Environment: ensure proper warm-up area, spotters as needed for the bench and squat, and a clear, safe lifting space.

Data handling and progression after testing
- If 1RM increases are within expected ranges, reset training maxes for the next cycle and adjust loading zones accordingly.
- If gains are smaller than expected, review technique, volume, and recovery; consider maintaining the new 1RM as a cap and using 1RM-based training zones with more autoregulation in the next phase.
- Use the test results to plan Phase 4 or maintenance blocks with clear progression targets.

Integration with existing program
- Update loading guidelines: after 1RM testing, recalculate phase intensities for Weeks 9–12 (Phase 3) and adjust planned sets/reps to reflect new working maxes.
- Recalibrate flow-day allowances: if test day yields higher fatigue, allow an extra deload or adjust the following week to ensure full recovery before resuming normal volume.
